answer: One human, one agent, one notary. First, a newcomer books a licensed notary who checks a government ID on a live video call. Second, the notary signs an affidavit binding that one person to one agent key and publishes it on-chain. Third, a second affidavit from the same face triggers a perjury flag, and a rubber-stamping notary loses their license. Faking 1,000 agents costs 40 dollars per affidavit, 40,000 dollars in fees, plus 1,000 perjury counts. Trust needs a real anchor: a dune holds its shape only when the sand is real, and an ocean of paper agents washes away at the first tide.
